description:
The pet's windows (§7.1) and nothing else: they may receive host events and start an operating-system drag of themselves, and they may not read a file, open a dialog, raise a notification, or move a window in any other way.

**`core:window:allow-start-dragging` is that drag, and it is the whole of it.** It is what `getWindowControls().startDragging()` needs (`platform/window.ts`), and it is what both of the pet's surfaces call: the ball through `PetFloatingBall.vue` and the character through `DesktopPetRoot.vue`, each asking the compositor once per gesture. §7.3's ban on per-frame IPC is therefore satisfied by construction rather than by discipline, and no position, geometry or monitor permission is granted to either window — a drag that needed one would not be this design, because the compositor owns the movement from the moment it starts. `desktop-pet-ball.json` names `pet-ball` and grants the same permission; it was written when the ball was the only surface that could move, and its own description says what its narrowing was for.

**Nine of the app's own commands**, one per call the pet's own page and menu make — and the ninth
is the one that answers with the *app's* appearance rather than the pet's (`desktop_pet_host_appearance`:
the theme, colour scheme, accent, contrast and body size the main window is drawing with, published by
`desktop_pet_publish_host_appearance` and held by `desktop_pet/host_appearance.rs`). It is granted here
because a pet window has to draw the same palette the app is in, and it is deliberately *not* the way
that value is written: the write is a command `main` alone holds, so a decoration can read what the app
looks like and can never say it. The direction is what §5.3's 「事件不能作为无需授权的配置写入口」
asks for, and this file is where the read half of it is stated: `desktop_pet_state` (the lifecycle's first read), `desktop_pet_set_visible` (the menu's hide), `desktop_pet_close_own` and `desktop_pet_set_click_through` (its own window, and only its own — both take the caller Tauri reports rather than a label), `desktop_pet_open_settings` (the menu's settings, which names a page and never a window), `desktop_pet_tasks` (the task feed's first read and every re-read after a push), `desktop_pet_appearance` (what the window draws, which resolves one sheet file and no directory), `desktop_pet_host_appearance` (the app's own appearance, described above), and `desktop_pet_open_task` (the bubble's click, which names a task and never a window).

Deliberately absent, and each for a reason a reader can check: every `agent_*` (a decoration does not start, stop, prompt or authorise a run), every `fs_*` (it reads no vault file), `desktop_pet_open` and `desktop_pet_disable` (creating and tearing down character windows is the settings switch's job, not a decoration's — a pet that could open more pets is a second way to reach the cap), `desktop_pet_windows` and `desktop_pet_capabilities` (the settings page's reports), `desktop_pet_read_settings`/`desktop_pet_update_settings` (writing `general.characterWindow` or `general.ball` is the switch itself, and the sizes the windows are built at ride the same write), and `desktop_pet_library`/`desktop_pet_import_character` (the character picker and the import dialog, which are the settings page's and which the pet does not need to draw the character it was already told to draw).
